jp: 誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}教室[きょうしつ]{の|no-possessive}窓[まど]{を|o-object}開[あ]けました{か|ka-question}。
en: Who opened the classroom window?
why: A question word that is the doer of the action is marked with が; the window is the object, so it takes を.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]図書館[としょかん]{で|de-place}日本語[にほんご]{を|o-object}勉強[べんきょう]します。
en: I study Japanese at the library every day.
why: 日本語 is what is being studied, the direct object of 勉強する, so it takes を.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{は|wa-topic}英語[えいご]{が|ga-stative}上手[じょうず]です。
en: Mr. Tanaka is good at English.
why: 上手 is a state adjective whose target is marked with が, never を.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}数学[すうがく]{が|ga-stative}好[す]きです。
en: I like math.
why: The thing liked with 好き is marked with が; 好き is an adjective, not a verb taking を.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{が/は|ga-subject}黒板[こくばん]{を|o-object}消[け]しました。
en: The teacher erased the blackboard.
why: The blackboard is what the teacher acted on, the direct object of 消す, so it takes を.

jp: 教室[きょうしつ]{に|ni-location}学生[がくせい]{が|ga-existence}十人[じゅうにん]います。
en: There are ten students in the classroom.
why: What exists is marked with が when you say it is present with いる; いる never takes を.

jp: 机[つくえ]{の|no-possessive}上[うえ]{に|ni-location}辞書[じしょ]{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There is a dictionary on the desk.
why: With あります the thing that exists is marked with が, not を.

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]{で|de-place}毎日[まいにち]資料[しりょう]{を|o-object}作[つく]ります。
en: I make documents at the company every day.
why: The documents are what gets made, the object of 作る, so they take を.

jp: 部長[ぶちょう]{が/は|ga-subject}会議室[かいぎしつ]{で|de-place}電話[でんわ]{を|o-object}かけています。
en: The department head is making a phone call in the meeting room.
why: 電話をかける is a fixed verb-object phrase: the call is the object of かける, so it takes を.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{の|no-possessive}説明[せつめい]{が|ga-stative}分[わ]かりません。
en: I don't understand the teacher's explanation.
why: 分かる marks the thing understood with が; 分かる never takes を.

jp: 昨日[きのう]{は|wa-topic}宿題[しゅくだい]{を|o-object}しませんでした。
en: I didn't do my homework yesterday.
why: The homework is the object of the verb する, so it takes を.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}漢字[かんじ]{が|ga-stative}嫌[きら]いです。
en: My younger brother dislikes kanji.
why: The thing disliked with 嫌い is marked with が; it is an adjective and takes no を.

jp: 同僚[どうりょう]{が/は|ga-subject}私[わたし]{の|no-possessive}仕事[しごと]{を|o-object}手伝[てつだ]ってくれました。
en: A colleague helped me with my work.
why: The work is what the colleague helped with, the object of 手伝う, so it takes を.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{に|ni-recipient}質問[しつもん]{を|o-object}しました。
en: I asked the teacher a question.
why: 質問をする makes the question the object of する, so it takes を.

jp: 授業[じゅぎょう]{が/は|ga-subject}九時[くじ]{に|ni-time}始[はじ]まります。
en: The class starts at nine.
why: 始まる is intransitive, so the thing that starts is its subject and takes が, never を.

jp: 試験[しけん]{が/は|ga-subject}やっと終[お]わりました。
en: The exam has finally ended.
why: 終わる is intransitive, so what ends is the subject and takes が rather than を.

jp: 学生[がくせい]{が|ga-subject}廊下[ろうか]{を|o-path}走[はし]っています。
en: A student is running along the corridor.
why: The corridor is the path travelled with 走る, which is marked with を; が would make the corridor the runner.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{は|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]コーヒー{を|o-object}飲[の]みます。
en: Mr. Tanaka drinks coffee every morning.
why: The coffee is what is drunk, the object of 飲む, so it takes を.

jp: 駅[えき]{の|no-possessive}近[ちか]く{に|ni-location}学校[がっこう]{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There is a school near the station.
why: With あります the thing that exists takes が; あります does not take を.

jp: 社長[しゃちょう]{が/は|ga-subject}明日[あした]大阪[おおさか]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: The company president is going to Osaka tomorrow.
why: The president is the one who goes; the doer of an intransitive verb like 行く takes が.

jp: 教科書[きょうかしょ]{を|o-object}家[いえ]{に|ni-location}忘[わす]れました。
en: I left my textbook at home.
why: The textbook is what I forgot, the object of 忘れる, so it takes を.

jp: 隣[となり]{の|no-possessive}教室[きょうしつ]{から|kara-from}歌[うた]{が|ga-sense}聞[き]こえます。
en: A song can be heard from the next classroom.
why: With the spontaneous verb 聞こえる, the sound that reaches you is marked with が.

jp: 窓[まど]{から|kara-from}山[やま]{が|ga-sense}見[み]えます。
en: You can see the mountains from the window.
why: 見える means something comes into view by itself, so the thing seen takes が.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{の|no-possessive}話[はなし]{を|o-object}よく聞[き]いてください。
en: Please listen carefully to the teacher's talk.
why: 聞く is a deliberate action, so what you listen to is its object and takes を.

jp: 誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}答[こた]え{を|o-object}知[し]っています{か|ka-question}。
en: Who knows the answer?
why: The question word asks who the knower is, so it is the subject and takes が.

jp: 図書館[としょかん]{で|de-place}本[ほん]{を|o-object}借[か]りました。
en: I borrowed a book at the library.
why: The book is what was borrowed, the object of 借りる, so it takes を.

jp: 教室[きょうしつ]{の|no-possessive}電気[でんき]{が|ga-subject}消[き]えています。
en: The classroom light is off.
why: 消える is intransitive: the light goes out by itself, so it is the subject and takes が.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{が/は|ga-subject}教室[きょうしつ]{の|no-possessive}電気[でんき]{を|o-object}消[け]しました。
en: The teacher turned off the classroom light.
why: 消す is transitive: the light is what the teacher switched off, so it takes を.

jp: 授業[じゅぎょう]{で|de-place}英語[えいご]{を|o-object}話[はな]します。
en: We speak English in class.
why: 英語 is what is spoken, the object of 話す, so it takes を.

jp: 先輩[せんぱい]{は|wa-topic}パソコン{が|ga-stative}得意[とくい]です。
en: My senior colleague is good with computers.
why: 得意 is a state adjective: what one is good at is marked with が, not を.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}仕事[しごと]{が|ga-subject}早[はや]く終[お]わりました。
en: Work ended early today.
why: 終わる is intransitive here, so the work that ended is the subject and takes が.

jp: 社員[しゃいん]{が/は|ga-subject}会議室[かいぎしつ]{に|ni-destination}集[あつ]まりました。
en: The employees gathered in the meeting room.
why: 集まる is intransitive, so the ones who gather are the subject and take が.

jp: 黒板[こくばん]{の|no-possessive}字[じ]{が|ga-sense}見[み]えません。
en: I can't see the writing on the blackboard.
why: 見えない reports what does not come into view, and that thing takes が.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{に|ni-recipient}宿題[しゅくだい]{を|o-object}出[だ]しました。
en: I handed in my homework to the teacher.
why: The homework is what was handed over, the object of 出す, so it takes を.

jp: 図書館[としょかん]{に|ni-location}留学生[りゅうがくせい]{が|ga-existence}たくさんいます。
en: There are a lot of international students in the library.
why: The people who are present with いる are marked with が; いる never takes を.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}日本語[にほんご]{が|ga-stative}少[すこ]し分[わ]かります。
en: I understand a little Japanese.
why: 分かる takes が for the thing understood, not を.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{が/は|ga-subject}学生[がくせい]{を|o-object}呼[よ]びました。
en: The teacher called the student over.
why: The student is the one called, the object of 呼ぶ, so the student takes を.

jp: 英語[えいご]{の|no-possessive}テスト{が|ga-existence}明日[あした]あります。
en: There is an English test tomorrow.
why: With ある the thing that takes place is marked with が, never を.

jp: 毎晩[まいばん]九時[くじ]{に|ni-time}日記[にっき]{を|o-object}書[か]きます。
en: I write in my diary at nine every evening.
why: The diary is what is written, the object of 書く, so it takes を.

jp: 母[はは]{が/は|ga-subject}学校[がっこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}来[き]ました。
en: My mother came to the school.
why: 来る is intransitive, so the person who came is the subject and takes が.

jp: 来週[らいしゅう]会社[かいしゃ]{で|de-place}面接[めんせつ]{を|o-object}受[う]けます。
en: I will have an interview at the company next week.
why: 面接を受ける: the interview is the object of 受ける, so it takes を.

jp: 先輩[せんぱい]{に|ni-source}仕事[しごと]{を|o-object}教[おし]えてもらいました。
en: I had my senior colleague teach me the job.
why: The job is what was taught, the object of 教える, so it takes を.

jp: 駅[えき]{で|de-place}友達[ともだち]{を|o-object}待[ま]っています。
en: I am waiting for my friend at the station.
why: 待つ takes the person waited for as its object, marked with を.

jp: 英語[えいご]{の|no-possessive}辞書[じしょ]{を|o-object}持[も]っています{か|ka-question}。
en: Do you have an English dictionary?
why: The dictionary is what is held, the object of 持つ, so it takes を.

jp: 新[あたら]しい辞書[じしょ]{が|ga-stative}ほしいです。
en: I want a new dictionary.
why: ほしい is an adjective, and the thing wanted is marked with が rather than を.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}学校[がっこう]{で|de-place}サッカー{を|o-object}します。
en: My younger brother plays soccer at school.
why: サッカーをする: the sport is the object of する, so it takes を.

jp: 同僚[どうりょう]{が/は|ga-subject}風邪[かぜ]{で|de-cause}仕事[しごと]{を|o-object}休[やす]みました。
en: A colleague took time off work because of a cold.
why: 仕事を休む: the work being missed is the object of 休む, so it takes を.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{の|no-possessive}声[こえ]{が|ga-sense}後[うし]ろ{の|no-possessive}席[せき]{から|kara-from}聞[き]こえません。
en: I can't hear the teacher's voice from the back seats.
why: 聞こえる (can be heard) marks the sound that reaches you with が, not を.
